title: Access updates from October 1-14, 2026
disclaimer: This dated retrospective preserves what the cited reports said on their stated dates. It is not a claim that every condition remained current after those reports or that coverage was complete.

items.title: Volunteer EMS authority was still suspended in the September 29 status described by the October 1 report
items.summary: Fluvanna Review's October 1 report described volunteer emergency medical services authority as still suspended on September 29 in Palmyra, Kents Store and Fork Union after a September 11 suspension. County-paid EMS remained operational; the report said the suspension could last up to 45 days, with earlier restoration possible.

items.title: Hickory Villa closure plan set resident moves before October 16
items.summary: Flatwater Free Press reported that Bethesda planned to close Hickory Villa and move residents before October 16. The report does not establish completion or resident outcomes; Hickory Villa is separate from Cambridge Court.

items.title: Winchester Family Medicine announced a planned permanent closure
items.summary: An official Cheshire Medical Center notice announced that the Winchester Family Medicine office at 20 Warwick Road would permanently close and said its sole provider, Lisa Moulton, would leave on November 6. The first patient letter was mailed October 14; transfers were not reported as complete, and the notice does not establish the sequence of closure and departure.

items.title: Dennys River Ambulance planned an end-of-November shutdown
items.summary: Maine Public reported that Dennys River Ambulance Service planned to close at the end of November after more than 60 years, citing insufficient volunteers. Replacement arrangements were uncertain in the report; no measured response-time outcome is claimed.

items.title: CMS planned to terminate Tender Home Health's Medicare provider agreement
items.summary: CMS listed a planned October 24 termination of Tender Home Health's Medicare provider agreement for substantial noncompliance. This is a provider-participation action, not evidence of business or facility closure.
